newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Rajasthan state clears two power projects.
newsitem.headline: India's Rajasthan state clears two power projects.

text.p: India's western state of Rajasthan has approved two power projects that will together generate more than 1,200 mega watts of electricity, the state chief minister said.
A 788.5 mega watt naptha-based project will be set up by India's R.P. Goenka group (RPG) in the state's Bikaner district.
The project will cost about $800 million, chief minister Bhairon Singh Sekhawat said.

The other project, 500 mw naptha-based, has been bagged by a consortium of four firms -- Pacific Corporation of the U.S., Rheinbraun AG and Vereinigte Energiewerke AG of Germany and India's Hindustan Development Corporation.
This project will also cost about $800 million, Sekhawat said.
The consortium has promised to generate power at a cost of 6.04 U.S. cents per unit.
The RPG group which runs a successful electricity generating firm, CESC Ltd, for the city of Calcutta, has promised to generate power at 5.97 cents per unit.
